weekly.headline: Attack agents found a zero-day — and AWS rewired identity
weekly.intro: The week's security news kept circling one question: what happens when the thing holding your credentials isn't a person.

themes.title: Attack agents found a zero-day without a human
themes.takeaway: Treat basic hygiene — patching, exposed services, credential reuse — as urgent; AI agents now find and exploit the flaws you deferred, at machine speed.
themes.detail: Amazon Threat Intelligence published an investigation into a Chinese-nexus actor whose "Cairn" agents were given the goal "obtain shell access" and discovered a zero-day with minimal human involvement. The UK's NCSC warned the same week that AI-driven attacks are mostly exposing years of weak foundations rather than novel techniques, and FortiGuard Labs counted more than 4,400 malicious holiday-shopping domains aimed at credential theft.

articles.title: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
Fake Delivery Notices, Stolen Logins, and Malicious Domains Threaten Holiday Shoppers

themes.title: AWS rebuilds IAM around non-human callers
themes.takeaway: You can now give an AI agent a narrower, attributable credential than the role it inherited — adopt this before agents ship with standing permissions.
themes.detail: AWS Sign-In added Enterprise-Managed Authorization using the ID-JAG grant, so Okta and other IdPs can authorize agents reaching the AWS MCP Server. Alongside it: a new STS GetScopedCredentials API that trims permissions on an existing session, Cognito token exchange for OAuth-style user delegation, and trusted identity propagation that carries the human or workload behind an IAM role into authorization and audit records.

articles.title: Secure agentic access to AWS with Enterprise-Managed Authorization
Scope down permissions of existing sessions using AWS STS GetScopedCredentials
Know the identity behind the role: Authorize and audit with trusted identity propagation

themes.title: Claude Ship lets agents approve the pull request
themes.takeaway: Branch protection and CI gates are now the only thing between agent-approved changes and main, so audit them before anyone enables agentic approvals.
themes.detail: Anthropic released Claude Ship, which lets agents review, fix and approve routine code changes rather than just propose them. Docker's AI Governance takes the opposite tack, constraining what network, filesystem, credential and MCP access a coding agent gets and giving teams a way to test that the limits hold; GitHub published a Copilot agent skill for picking bounded, reversible legacy modernisation steps.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
Prove your AI agent guardrails work
How to choose the next safe step in application modernization

themes.title: AWS WAF repricing lands February 1, 2027
themes.takeaway: Re-forecast your WAF spend now: billing shifts to resources protected, traffic inspected and protection level, with existing customers migrated automatically in February 2027.
themes.detail: In the same batch, AWS Network Firewall gained context-aware rules that match on VPCs, subnets, security groups and transit gateway attachments instead of IP ranges, a Next Generation policy combining allow-listing with threat inspection, and a preview mode that applies central rules at each VPC's internet gateway. Lambda's timeout also doubled to 30 minutes — its first change since 2018 — and it now runs on GPUs.

articles.title: Introducing AWS WAF simplified pricing

themes.title: Sovereignty plans that assume the cloud stays up
themes.takeaway: Only 3% of IT teams could operate through a cloud cutoff — a gap your DR tests should close before the next multi-day Outlook-class outage.
themes.detail: Futurum Research's "Sovereignty is Control, Not Location" found governance committees and NIS2/DORA compliance work have not translated into operational resilience. The past fortnight brought a multi-day Outlook outage, a JPMorgan Chase failure, an FAA ground stop and a Delta weight-and-balance system outage in Atlanta. Red Hat separately argues the automation platform itself — Ansible Automation Platform — needs its own HA and DR plan.
